messages:
anika: Quick RFC follow-up — I prototyped a slotless scheduler that uses a small 'pacing window' + admission watermark. Want to discuss tradeoffs and a minimal backpressure API for the runtime.
ryan: sketch it out pls.
anika: Main idea: remove per-slot accounting. Keep per-tenant pacing_score and a rolling window estimate of in-flight token consumption. Admission rule is simple: admit if (window_tokens + predicted_tail) <= tenant_alloc_headroom else suggest delay.
maria: How do we handle preemption? If we don't have explicit slots we need a way to avoid long-tail starvation when a big burst starts.
sasha: My worry: fairness under bursty tenants. Without discrete slots, bursts could push out many small low-priority requests unless pacing window decays fast.
ken: Operational question — can we expose backpressure to upper layers? Something like a tiny queryable endpoint so control-plane or SDKs can adapt.
anika: Proposed tiny API (runtime):
```
GET /runtime/backpressure?tenant_id=...
# response (proto): { state: STRING, headroom_tokens: INT64, recommended_delay_ms: INT32 }
```
Also allow attaching `deadline_hint` metadata on the request to help admission prioritize.
ryan: :thumbsup: I prefer recommended_delay vs hard reject. We should also support an opt-in `soft_reserve` flag for very low-latency ops that can borrow headroom and be accounted later.
sasha: Soft-reserve is basically per-request priority tokens. Adds complexity to admission but could be limited to whitelisted tenants.
maria: For observability we'll need: headroom_gauge, queue_depth_by_priority, avg_delay_ms, p95/p99 delay, reject_rate_by_tenant.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary slotless-scheduler v0.2 deployed to dev cluster 'dev-a' at 2750012358
anika: Rollout plan proposal: opt-in pool-level switch -> 2-week canary with synthetic workloads + replay. Gate on 95p latency and token-cost delta. If p95 latency regresses >5% or cost rises >4% then rollback.
ken: Another interaction: KV cache churn. With slotless admission many small requests might evict hot KV entries. We should tie cache TTL to pacing_score or request_size_estimate.
ryan: TTL idea: ttl = base_ttl * (1 + burst_factor). Burst_factor derived from short-term request rate.
sasha: Edge case: long-lived streaming sessions. Treat streaming as a separate flow: allocate streaming_window = active_streams * per_stream_rate and keep them out of the short-request pacing pool.
anika: Good catch. Also thinking about a "grace headroom" bucket that decays over time to allow short bursts without immediate rejection.
maria: I'll build perf scenarios to simulate: steady load, spike, multi-tenant cross-traffic, and KV-churn. Need hooks to control per-tenant burst_factor.
ken: I'll own canary config and the opt-in rollout toggles.
ryan: I'll prototype the /runtime/backpressure endpoint and add a small dashboard tile showing recommended_delay and headroom.
anika: I'll draft the follow-up RFC with API proto, rollout playbook, and perf targets. Anyone want to pair on the perf harness this week?
maria: I can pair EOW on p95/p99 sims.
ken: I'll set up the canary flags.
ryan: I'll push a tiny PR with the endpoint stub (will add unit tests + basic telemetry).
anika: Thanks — filing RFC PR: https://git.redwood/repo/rfcs/slotless-pacing (WIP). Will include sample traces and a simulation report.
